$$

from the corresponding Fourier series of $f(x).$The Fourier series of $f(x)$ is given by

$$

$$

Since $f$ is 
{{field-2}} 
on $R,$ we may integrate its Fourier series term-by-term to get

$$
4{x}^{2}∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{{field-3}}\cdot {{field-4}}.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that $F(x)$ is an odd function. So, the Fourier series of its $2L$-periodic extension has the form

$$
{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{L}).
$$

In our case, $L=2$ and we are already given the coefficients ${b}_{n}$ for $n\ge 1.$ Thus, the Fourier series of $f(x)$ is given by

$$
f(x)∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{32(-1)^{n+1}}{n\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2}).
$$

Now, notice that the function $F$ is continuous on $(-2,2).$ 
Therefore, the $4$-periodic extension $f$ is $\text{piecewise continuous}$ on $R,$ so we may integrate its Fourier series term-by-term:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{x}8t\,\text{d}t & ∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{\int }_{0}^{x}\frac{32(-1)^{n+1}}{n\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi t}{2})\,\text{d}t \\ [4{t}^{2}]_{0}^{x} & ∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{32(-1)^{n+1}}{n\pi }\cdot [-\frac{2}{n\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi t}{2})]_{0}^{x} \\ 4{x}^{2} & ∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\,\frac{64(-1)^{n+1}}{{n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}}\cdot (1-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2}))\end{aligned}
$$

$$

questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that $F(x)$ is an even function. So, the Fourier series of its $2L$-periodic extension has the form

$$
\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{L}).
$$

In our case, $L=3$ and we are already given the coefficients ${a}_{0}$ and ${a}_{n}$ for $n\ge 1.$ Thus, the Fourier series of $f(x)$ is given by

$$
f(x)∼-17+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{252(-1)^{n+1}}{{n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{3}).
$$

Now, notice that 

- the function $F$ is continuously differentiable on $(-3,3),$

- continuous on $[-3,3),$ and

- satisfies $F(-3)=F(3),$ if we extend the value at $x=3$ using the formula $F(x)=-7{x}^{2}+4.$

Therefore, the $6$-periodic extension $f$ is $\text{continuous}$ and $\text{piecewise smooth}$ on $R,$ so we may differentiate its Fourier series term-by-term:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-7{x}^{2}+4) & ∼\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-17)+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{252(-1)^{n+1}}{{n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{3})) \\ -14x & ∼0+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{252(-1)^{n+1}}{{n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}}\cdot (-\frac{n\pi }{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{3})) \\ -14x & ∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{-84(-1)^{n+1}}{n\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{3}) \\ -14x & ∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\,\frac{84(-1)^{n}}{n\pi }\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{3})\end{aligned}
$$
